articles.title: Ajit Agarkar Replaced! BCCI Names Pragyan Ojha Chief Selector, Ramesh Powar Joins Panel
articles.description: The BCCI has reshaped its men’s senior selection panel, appointing former India spinner Ramesh Powar as a selector and elevating Pragyan Ojha to the chairperson’s role following Ajit Agarkar’s departure. The appointments follow a selection process conducted by the board’s Cricket Advisory Committee (CAC), which interviewed applicants at the BCCI headquarters before recommending Powar for the vacant position. Ramesh Powar Joins BCCI Men’s Selection Committee Powar’s appointment brings a former India international with experience in both playing and coaching to the men’s selection panel. The Mumbai-born spinner represented India in two Tests and 31 ODIs during his international career. After retiring from international cricket, Powar moved into coaching and held several prominent roles. He served as head coach of the India women’s team, as well as Mumbai and Gujarat, and also worked as a bowling coach at the BCCI Centre of Excellence. His stint with the India women’s team included an Asia Cup title and a silver medal at the Commonwealth Games. That experience across domestic and international cricket adds another dimension to the selection committee as it evaluates players for India’s upcoming assignments. The CAC, comprising Ashok Malhotra and Jatin Paranjape, conducted the interviews and unanimously recommended Powar for the role, according to the BCCI’s announcement. Pragyan Ojha Takes Over As Chief Selector Alongside Powar’s appointment, the BCCI confirmed that Pragyan Ojha will serve as chairperson of the men’s senior selection committee, succeeding Agarkar. The chairperson’s position is determined by seniority, with the number of Test appearances for India forming the basis of the decision. Ojha’s record gives him the required seniority among the panel members. Agarkar’s tenure ended earlier this month after he opted against seeking a contract extension. During his time in charge, India won three ICC titles, making the change in leadership a notable development for the national team’s selection setup. Ojha will now lead the committee as it takes decisions on squad composition, player selection and India’s preparations for future international competitions. Full List Of BCCI Men’s Senior Selection Committee Members The reconstituted panel comprises five members, with Ojha taking over as chairperson and Powar filling the vacant position. Pragyan Ojha (Chairperson) Shiv Sundar Das RP Singh Ajay Ratra Ramesh Powar The new committee brings together former India internationals with experience across different formats and coaching environments. Its decisions will shape the composition of India’s men’s squads as the team moves into its next phase of international cricket.

articles.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
articles.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks.
